entries.card_text: People don't want to be in crowded spaces.

none_rationale.text: "crowded spaces" concerns how full a place is; it matches no definitional element of the eight characteristics.

quotes: don't want to be in crowded spaces
rationale.text: States a preference about being in spaces but no effect on how many places exist; reaching Quantity needs unstated steps (avoidance, then less use, then closure). Being in a space is most directly a matter of use.

quotes: People don't want to be in crowded spaces
rationale.text: A condition (a preference) with no stated effect on anything; no causal relation.
Presented as a standing preference; no change language and nothing implying the preference shifted.
A preference is a Psychology variable, but no causal relation is stated (mechanism 0), so, as with a bare label, the lens is indicated by vocabulary but no causal work can be assessed.

quotes: don't want to be in crowded spaces
rationale.text: The effect is not stated; one element (avoidance of crowded places) must be supplied before an implication follows.

testability.testable_implication: If people do not want to be in crowded spaces, one would expect crowded third places to lose more visitors than uncrowded ones, compared with no difference by crowding.
testability.implication_note: Supplied element: the effect, read as avoidance of crowded places.

rationale.text: Names a subset of places (crowded ones); the card would not apply to places that are not crowded.

scope.stated_scope: crowded spaces
scope.bodo_question: Do third places in a small city reach the levels of crowding the card has in mind, and would gatherings organised through clubs be affected in the same way?

entries.card_text: Social media isolation (bad reputation given by influencers)

none_rationale.text: Neither "isolation" nor a "bad reputation" matches a definitional element of any characteristic; the card does not say what has the bad reputation.

rationale.text: Two noun phrases with no stated effect; the filing position is the only link to the number of places. No other claim is a more direct fit, because no effect is stated.
Bare noun phrases; no effect on third places and no pathway is stated.
"isolation" can denote a state or a process; the card does not state that social media use or influencer reputation changed.

Isolation and reputation (perception) are Psychology variables, but no causal relation is stated (mechanism 0), so, as with a bare label, the lens is indicated by vocabulary but no causal work can be assessed.
The card does not say what has the bad reputation or what follows from it; the analyst would have to supply both effect and pathway.

testability.implication_note: No effect or pathway is stated; deriving an implication would mean writing the explanation for the student.

rationale.text: Influencers and social media are actors whose presence varies, which implies but does not state a scope.

scope.stated_scope: Implied: settings where social media and influencers shape reputations.
scope.bodo_question: Would reputations formed by influencers bear on third places in a small city, where people may know the places directly, and would club-based places be affected in the same way?

entries.analyst_note: Workbook note: first letter of 'media' obscured by pin; reading not in doubt, so no caveat.

entries.card_text: They aren't economically viable. The don't make enough revenue. They don't break even, harder to stay in business.

none_rationale.text: The card concerns revenue and viability; it describes no definitional element of any characteristic.

rationale.text: Staying in business is the Quantity variable directly: places that cannot stay in business close.
Cause (insufficient revenue) leads to a stated intermediate (not breaking even) and then to the effect (harder to stay in business).
"harder" implies a shift, but the card does not state that revenue or costs changed.
Revenue and break-even are Economics variables and do all the causal work.
Cause, effect and direction are stated concretely enough for an implication without additions.

testability.testable_implication: If insufficient revenue is closing third places, one would expect places that close to show revenue below their costs in the period before closure, compared with places that stay open.

rationale.text: "They" refers to third places in general; no subset or condition is named.

scope.bodo_question: Does the revenue pressure the card describes apply in the same way to third places run through clubs or supported in a welfare-state setting as to purely commercial ones?

entries.analyst_note: 'harder to stay in business' was added in smaller writing (workbook note); it is student text and is quoted.

entries.card_text: Lack of funding because of corruption or bad location.

none_rationale.text: "bad location" is linked by the card to funding, not to ease of access; it does not describe the Accessibility definition's "easy to access" (the Accessibility counter-indicator's "out-of-the-way location" was considered and not applied for that reason).

rationale.text: States lack of funding but not its effect on the number of places; the step from funding to closure is unstated.

quotes: Lack of funding because of corruption or bad location
rationale.text: A causal relation is stated ("because of") from corruption or location to lack of funding, with no intermediate step and no stated effect on places.
A level ("Lack") stated without change language; corruption and bad location are presented as standing conditions.
Funding is the Economics variable closest to the claim, but corruption (an abuse of power, a Politics variable) shares the causal work as one of the two stated causes.
Causes and their direction are stated; the effect of lack of funding on the number of places must be supplied.

testability.testable_implication: If lack of funding caused by corruption or bad location is reducing the number of third places, one would expect places in badly located areas or where corruption affects funding to close more often than comparable places, compared with no difference.
testability.implication_note: Supplied element: the effect, read as closure of underfunded places.

rationale.text: Names conditions (corruption, badly located places) such that the card would not apply where they are absent.

scope.stated_scope: Places affected by corruption or in bad locations.
scope.bodo_question: How would location bear on third places in a small city, and does the funding route the card assumes apply to club-based places in a welfare-state setting?

entries.analyst_note: 'and' struck through and replaced with 'OR' (workbook note); the struck word is not coded.

entries.card_text: Decrease in budget: relocation of money to other sectors. Also politics.

none_rationale.text: A budget decrease describes no definitional element of any characteristic.

rationale.text: States a budget decrease but not whose budget or its effect on the number of places; the step to closure is unstated.

quotes: relocation of money to other sectors
rationale.text: The colon links the decrease to a cause (money relocated elsewhere); no intermediate step and no stated effect on places.
"Decrease" is explicit change language.
The budget decrease is economic, but the relocation is a spending decision the card itself hands partly to another lens ("Also politics").

quotes: relocation of money to other sectors
rationale.text: Cause and direction are stated; the effect on the number of places (and whose budget) must be read in as one element.

testability.testable_implication: If budgets for third places are being cut by moving money to other sectors, one would expect closures to follow budget reductions for third places, compared with budgets that held steady.
testability.implication_note: Supplied element: the effect, read as the budget funding third places, whose decrease leads to closures.

rationale.text: A budget-holding institution that allocates money between sectors is implied, not stated.

scope.stated_scope: Implied: places dependent on a budget allocated across sectors.
scope.bodo_question: In a welfare-state setting, how far do third places depend on budgets allocated between sectors, and does that apply to places run through clubs?

entries.analyst_note: A short scribbled word struck through above 'also politics' (workbook note); not coded.

entries.card_text: High cost of living means need to work instead of socilise.

none_rationale.text: Socialising is not itself a characteristic; the card concerns people's time, not whether a place is easy to access or accommodates visitors' schedules.

rationale.text: The stated effect is on how people use their time (Usage). Reaching fewer places needs an unstated step (less use, then less revenue, then closure).
Cause (high cost of living) leads to a stated intermediate (need to work) and then to the effect (less socialising).
A level ("High") stated without change language; on its wording the condition could always have held.
Cost of living and the allocation of time to paid work are Economics variables.

quotes: need to work instead of socilise
rationale.text: Cause, effect and direction are stated.

testability.testable_implication: If a high cost of living pushes people to work instead of socialising, one would expect people facing higher living costs relative to income to spend more time working and less time socialising, compared with people facing lower living costs.

rationale.text: The cause is stated as a general condition; no population or setting is delimited.

scope.bodo_question: Does a welfare-state setting change how living costs translate into working time, and would time for club-based activity be squeezed in the same way?

entries.analyst_note: One word struck through after 'means' (workbook note); not coded.

entries.card_text: More recognized brands like Starbucks receive more money than the local brands.

none_rationale.text: The card concerns brands as businesses competing for money; it does not describe décor or branding inside places (the Low Profile counter-indicator's "visible branding" was considered and not applied).

quotes: receive more money than the local brands
rationale.text: States a revenue difference between chains and local brands, not an effect on the number of places; the step to closures is unstated.

quotes: More recognized brands like Starbucks receive more money
rationale.text: Relates brand recognition to receiving more money, with no intermediate step and no stated effect on places.
"More" compares brands with each other, not over time; presented as a standing condition.
Brands competing for revenue are Economics variables.

quotes: receive more money than the local brands
rationale.text: Cause, effect and contrast are on the card.

testability.testable_implication: If recognised brands receive more money than local ones, one would expect chain cafés such as Starbucks to take a larger share of spending than local cafés in the same area, compared with equal shares.

rationale.text: Scope is stated by contrast: settings where recognised brands compete with local ones; it would not apply where no such competition exists.

scope.stated_scope: Settings where recognised chains compete with local brands.
scope.bodo_question: Does a chain-versus-local contrast arise in a small city, and does it bear on third places organised through club-based civil society rather than commercial cafés?

entries.card_text: Conservative governments have underinvested in third places.

none_rationale.text: Investment describes no definitional element of any characteristic.

rationale.text: Underinvestment could reduce the number of places or the quality of those that remain; the effect fits Quantity and Quality equally and is not stated.
Relates a type of government to underinvestment, with no intermediate step and no stated effect on places.
Investment can vary over time and "have underinvested" implies a period, but the card does not say investment fell or that such governments became more common.
Governments and public spending decisions are Politics variables (Section 3.2).

quotes: Conservative governments have underinvested in third places
rationale.text: Cause, effect and direction are stated.

testability.testable_implication: If conservative governments underinvest in third places, one would expect public investment in third places to be lower under conservative governments than under others, compared with no difference by governing party.

rationale.text: Names a condition (conservative government) such that the card would not apply under other governments.

scope.stated_scope: Jurisdictions governed by conservative governments.
scope.bodo_question: In a welfare-state setting, does the party in government change investment in community space, and do club-based third places depend on such investment?

entries.card_text: Polarization

none_rationale.text: A single word; it describes no definitional element of any characteristic.

rationale.text: Bare label; no effect stated, so the filing position is the only link.
Single word; no effect or pathway stated.
Can denote either a state or a process (Section 8.3).
Bare label in the vocabulary of collective conflict and ideology (Politics); no causal work can be assessed.
Any implication would need the analyst to supply what polarisation affects and how.

testability.implication_note: Bare label; no effect or pathway to derive an implication from.

rationale.text: No scope cue.

scope.bodo_question: Is there reason to expect polarisation to operate in a small city's civic life as the card assumes, and would it reach club-based places?

entries.card_text: Modernisation: physical 3d places are declining because virtual ones are more available & other forms of entertainment.

none_rationale.text: Availability of virtual places and other entertainment describes no definitional element of the eight characteristics; digital spaces are coded against the eight only (Appendix A, A4).

rationale.text: "declining" does not say whether in number or in use; the effect fits Quantity and Usage equally, so no claim is a more direct fit.

quotes: physical 3d places are declining because virtual ones are more available
rationale.text: A cause (more available virtual places and other entertainment) and an effect (decline) are joined by "because", with no intermediate step such as substitution stated.
"more available" and "declining" are explicit change language.
The causal work is done by the availability of alternatives; no mental state, preference or motivation is named, so the Psychology lens is absent and the variable fits no lens in Section 3.2.
Cause and direction are stated, but "declining" is vague (number or use); its meaning must be supplied.

testability.testable_implication: If greater availability of virtual places and other entertainment draws people from physical third places, one would expect visits to physical third places to fall more among people with more access to virtual alternatives, compared with people with less access.
testability.implication_note: Supplied element: "declining" read as declining use, given the card's filing under Usage.

rationale.text: A process (modernisation) whose reach varies implies a scope: where virtual alternatives are available. Not stated.

scope.stated_scope: Implied: settings where virtual alternatives are available.
scope.bodo_question: Would virtual alternatives draw people from physical places in a small city in the same way, and would club-based gatherings be substituted as readily as other venues?

entries.analyst_note: Heading 'Modernisation' written once, struck through and rewritten (workbook note); the rewritten word is student text.

entries.card_text: People are becoming less collectively minded and more individualist. - social media, internet, talking to ai, modernisation - people don't have time for community because work.

none_rationale.text: "collectively minded" and "community" describe dispositions and time use, not a definitional element of any characteristic; "talking to ai" is talk outside a third place, not the Conversation definition's talk in one.

quotes: people don't have time for community because work
rationale.text: Time for "community" is close to use, but third places are not named; the step from less community time to less use of third places is unstated.

quotes: don't have time for community because work
rationale.text: A cause (work) and an effect (no time for community) are stated, with no intermediate step; the listed drivers of individualism are not linked to an effect.
"becoming less" and "more" are explicit change language.
Individualism is a Psychology variable, but the second mechanism runs through time allocated to work (Economics), which shares the causal work.

quotes: people don't have time for community because work
rationale.text: Cause, effect and direction are stated for the work mechanism.

testability.testable_implication: If work leaves people without time for community, one would expect people working longer hours to spend less time in community activity, compared with people working shorter hours.

quotes: People are becoming less collectively minded
rationale.text: "People" without qualification; no scope cue.

scope.bodo_question: Would a shift towards individualism be expected to hold in a small Northern Norwegian city, and how would it bear on participation in club-based civil society?

entries.card_text: Covid Adaptation: people become more introverted cause they got used to lock down.

none_rationale.text: Introversion describes no definitional element of any characteristic.

rationale.text: The stated effect is on people's disposition; the step from introversion to using third places less is unstated.
Cause (lockdown) leads to a stated intermediate (habituation, "got used to") and then to the effect (introversion).
"become more introverted" is explicit change; lockdown is a datable event.
Introversion (a trait) and habituation (a habit) are Psychology variables.

quotes: people become more introverted cause they got used to lock down
rationale.text: Cause, effect and direction are stated.

testability.testable_implication: If getting used to lockdown made people more introverted, one would expect people who experienced longer or stricter lockdowns to show a larger shift towards introversion, compared with people who experienced shorter or lighter ones.

rationale.text: An event whose presence and intensity varied (lockdown) implies a scope; not stated as one.

scope.stated_scope: Implied: populations that experienced lockdown.
scope.bodo_question: Would a lockdown-driven shift towards introversion be expected to persist in a small city, and would it reach participation in clubs?

entries.card_text: Some third places propose things that ppl can make themselves (for cheaper) -> coffee

quotes: propose things that ppl can make themselves
none_rationale.text: The card concerns what places sell and its home-made substitutes; it describes no definitional element of any characteristic.

rationale.text: Implies that people make the offer at home instead of going, which is less use of the place (Usage).

quotes: things that ppl can make themselves
rationale.text: Relates a home-makeable offer, cheaper at home, to the implied effect (people stay home); no stated pathway beyond the price contrast.
Presented as a standing condition; nothing says the offer, the price gap or home production changed.
Relative price and substitution by home production are Economics variables.
Cause, effect and contrast are on the card.

testability.testable_implication: If people substitute cheaper home-made versions, one would expect use to fall more at third places whose main offer can be made at home (such as coffee) than at places whose offer cannot.

quotes: Some third places propose things that ppl can make themselves
rationale.text: Names a subset of places (those whose offer can be made at home); it would not apply to others.

scope.stated_scope: Third places whose offer can be made more cheaply at home.
scope.bodo_question: Do the third places in question in a small city depend on selling something people can make at home, or are club-based places organised around something else?

entries.card_text: People are working more and for longer because of rising living costs and therefore don't have time to go to third places

quotes: don't have time to go to third places
none_rationale.text: The card concerns visitors' time, not whether a place is easy to access or accommodates visitors' schedules (the Accessibility definition); association only.

quotes: don't have time to go to third places
rationale.text: Going to third places less is the Usage variable directly.

quotes: don't have time to go to third places
rationale.text: Three linked steps: rising living costs, then longer working, then no time to go.
"rising" and "more" are explicit change language.
Living costs and the allocation of time to paid work are Economics variables.

quotes: don't have time to go to third places
rationale.text: Cause, effect and direction are stated.

testability.testable_implication: If rising living costs lengthen working hours and crowd out visits, one would expect people whose working hours rose with living costs to visit third places less often, compared with people whose hours did not rise.

rationale.text: "People" without qualification; the cause is stated as a general trend, not a delimited setting.

scope.bodo_question: Does a welfare-state setting change whether rising living costs lengthen working hours, and would time for club-based activity be squeezed in the same way?

entries.analyst_note: 'longer' partly obscured by pin (workbook note); reading not in doubt, so no caveat.

entries.card_text: There might [be] a hierarchy because nowadays third spaces are actually turning into business things eg: selling things; bringing ID
entries.transcription_caveat: '[be]' is a transcriber insertion and is not coded. The final word is read as 'ID' but is not certain; no code relies on it. If the final word were read with certainty, the Oldenburg mapping (for example Neutral Ground or The Leveler through an entry requirement) and the testable implication could change.

quotes: third spaces are actually turning into business things
rationale.text: "a hierarchy" in places describes rank or status carrying weight, the opposite of the Leveler definition; the card links it to places turning into businesses.
The stated effect is a hierarchy within places, a characteristic weakening (Quality); reaching less use needs an unstated step.

quotes: a hierarchy because nowadays third spaces are actually turning into business things
rationale.text: Cause (places turning into businesses) and effect (hierarchy) joined by "because"; the examples illustrate the cause but give no intermediate step.
"nowadays" and "turning into" are explicit change language.
Commercialisation (selling, business) is the causal variable and is economic; the hierarchy is the effect on the place, not a lens variable.
Cause and direction are stated, but "hierarchy" is vague; its meaning must be supplied.

testability.testable_implication: If places turning into businesses creates hierarchy, one would expect outside status to carry more weight among users of third places that have become more commercial, compared with places that have not.
testability.implication_note: Supplied element: "hierarchy" read in the Leveler sense, as outside rank or status carrying weight among users.

rationale.text: Places that have become commercial are implied as the scope; the card states the trend for third spaces generally.

scope.stated_scope: Implied: third places that have become commercial.
scope.bodo_question: Would a turn towards commercial operation apply to third places organised through clubs, and would it create hierarchy in a small-city setting where users may already know one another?

entries.card_text: Economics: Less disposable income for ticketed third spaces (museums etc)

quotes: Less disposable income for ticketed third spaces
rationale.text: Ticketed entry that people have less income for matches the Accessibility counter-indicator "a price point that restricts regular attendance" (Accessibility counter-indicator).

quotes: Less disposable income for ticketed third spaces
rationale.text: Less income available for ticketed places unambiguously implies fewer paid visits, the Usage variable.

quotes: Less disposable income for ticketed third spaces
rationale.text: A condition with a direction of effect (less income available for ticketed places), but no pathway is stated.
"Less" states a change in income.
Disposable income and ticket prices are Economics variables.
Cause, implied effect and the ticketed/non-ticketed contrast are on the card.

testability.testable_implication: If less disposable income reduces use of ticketed third spaces, one would expect visits to fall more at ticketed places such as museums than at free places among people whose disposable income fell, compared with people whose income did not.

rationale.text: Names a subset of places (ticketed ones); it would not apply to free places.

scope.stated_scope: Ticketed third spaces such as museums.
scope.bodo_question: Are the third places at issue in a small city ticketed at all, and how would a welfare-state setting bear on disposable income for paid entry to club-based places?

quotes: After math of political polecies from

testability.implication_note: No effect or pathway is stated in the legible text.

rationale.text: Policies apply where they were enacted, which implies but does not state a scope.

scope.stated_scope: Implied: wherever the policies applied.

entries.transcription_caveat: The final sentence ('If you [have?] the money.') is not reliably legible and is not coded. If it were read, it could add an economic condition, which could change lens fit (an Economics secondary lens) and scope.

none_rationale.text: Funding for communal activities and youth groups describes no definitional element of any characteristic.

quotes: Less funding for communal incentives, like youth groups

quotes: More right wing parties are winning elections
this is not something they prioritise

quotes: More right wing parties are winning

quotes: right wing parties are winning elections

quotes: right wing parties are winning elections

entries.card_text: Social anxiety and stress

rationale.text: Read without added words on the Outcomes claim, the card names a worsened social outcome rather than its cause.
Names a social consequence (anxiety, stress) of the kind Claim 3 says is worsening. Alternative reading (anxiety as a cause of less socialising) would require adding an effect; recorded, not adopted.
Bare noun phrase; no causal relation.
Named as states, with no change language.
Bare label in Psychology vocabulary (emotional states); no causal work can be assessed.
No cause and no pathway; the analyst would have to supply both.

testability.implication_note: Bare label naming an outcome; no explanation to derive an implication from.

rationale.text: No scope cue.

scope.bodo_question: Would the social anxiety and stress the card names be expected to show the same pattern in a small Northern Norwegian city, and would they bear on club-based gatherings?

entries.card_text: Social media massive consumption. Because people don't feel like they want to socialize anymore physically. & expectation

quotes: people don't feel like they want to socialize anymore physically

quotes: Because people don't feel like they want to socialize anymore physically

quotes: people don't feel like they want to socialize

entries.card_text: Workers earning a minimum wage is leading to demotivation.

none_rationale.text: Wages and motivation describe no definitional element of any characteristic.

rationale.text: Demotivation of workers is not itself a worse social or community outcome associated with third places; the link is unstated, and the card fits no other claim more directly.

quotes: Workers earning a minimum wage is leading to demotivation
rationale.text: Cause (minimum wage) and effect (demotivation) joined by "is leading to", with no intermediate step.
"is leading to" implies a shift in motivation, but the card does not state that wages changed.

quotes: Workers earning a minimum wage is leading to demotivation
rationale.text: Cause, effect and direction are stated.

testability.testable_implication: If earning a minimum wage leads to demotivation, one would expect workers on the minimum wage to report lower motivation than otherwise similar workers earning more, compared with no difference.

rationale.text: Names a population (minimum-wage workers); it would not apply to others.

scope.stated_scope: Workers earning a minimum wage.
scope.bodo_question: How would a welfare-state wage setting bear on demotivation among low-paid workers, and is that link relevant to social outcomes in club-based third places?

convergence.shared_mechanism: Less money is spent on third places or communal provision. S1-004 and S1-005 are filed Economics and coded Economics with Politics secondary; S1-008 and S1-018 are filed and coded Politics.

Paid work takes time that would otherwise go to socialising, community or third places. S1-006 and S1-014 are filed and coded Economics; S1-011 is filed Psychology (coded Psychology, with Economics secondary for this mechanism).

tensions.description: S1-001 attributes the decline to people not wanting to be in crowded spaces, which presumes places are busy; S1-003 attributes it to places not making enough revenue, which would follow from too few customers. As stated they predict opposite occupancy in places that close, unless crowding and low revenue occur at different times or in different places.

S1-003 states that third places in general are not economically viable; S1-007 states that recognised brands receive more money than local ones, implying viability differs by type of business. Both hold only if the chains are not counted as third places, which the theory file does not settle (Appendix A, A11).

gaps.notes: No Claim 1 card engages any characteristic. Five of the nine Claim 1 cards concern money (funding, budget, investment, revenue, brand revenue) but only S1-003 states an effect on the number of places; the others stop at the money. Both Psychology cards (S1-001, S1-002) state no causal relation; S1-001 and S1-006 state effects on use and are imported to Claim 2.
